theme: International arrivals: NTTO I-94, UNWTO, StatCan travellers, JNTO Japan, Korea KTO, Australia ABS overseas arrivals, Mexico INEGI/DATATUR, Brazil, Thailand MOTS, Indonesia BPS, India MoT
queries_run: gh search repos "inbound tourism statistics dataset"
gh search repos "JNTO Japan tourism statistics"
gh search repos "world tourism organization dataset" --sort updated
gh search repos "overseas arrivals departures Australia"

candidates.name: i94_immigration
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed files: sas_data.tar.xz (26.9MB, the classic US I-94 arrivals SAS extract, April 2016 only), immigration_data_sample.csv (144KB sample), I94_SAS_Labels_Descriptions.SAS (code labels for country/port/visa/mode/state fields), plus reference tables airlines.dat, airport-codes_csv.csv, airports.csv, cities.csv, countries.csv, mode.csv, visa.csv, us_states.csv, us-cities-demographics.csv. This is the Udacity Data Engineering capstone I-94 dataset (US National Travel & Tourism Office non-immigrant arrivals) with world-region/country, visa type, transport mode, age group, destination state, and port-of-entry fields. Also carries an unrelated GlobalLandTemperaturesByCity.parquet file (Kaggle climate data, ignore).
candidates.why_useful: We already hold current NTTO I-94 arrivals (per CONTEXT.md), but this is only a single month (Apr 2016) — value here is mainly the reference/crosswalk tables (visa code, mode-of-entry code, port/airport code, country code lookups) and a worked example of parsing the SAS I-94 extract, useful if the team ever needs to reprocess raw DHS/NTTO I-94 SAS files into a point-in-time panel (gap #4/#7). Low incremental data value, moderate tooling value.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: NTTO I-94 arrivals (already held) — this repo's actual arrivals data is older/narrower (one month, 2016) than what we hold
candidates.geography: United States (inbound, by country of origin)

candidates.name: iva-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics International Visitor Arrivals dashboard repo (description only inspected, not file-listed). Likely holds or pulls VBOS visitor arrival series for Vanuatu.
candidates.why_useful: Small Pacific-island market, not a listed priority country for ABNB (not in the 1-20 gap list explicitly), but a working example of a government-stats visitor-arrivals dashboard/pipeline that could be a template for building similar pulls for JNTO/KTO/ABS/DATATUR if none of those exist ready-made on GitHub.

candidates.name: tourism
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo description claims UNWTO World Tourism Barometer rankings (international visitor arrivals, inbound tourism revenue, outbound expenditure by UN region/subregion) but the actual repo content visible is just a README and a zipped 'TravelGuide-master.zip' — contents/provenance of the zip could not be confirmed without downloading it.
candidates.why_useful: If the zip does contain a UNWTO Barometer extract, it would directly address gap #7 (regional international arrivals) and the broader UNWTO ask in this theme; flagged for a human to unzip and verify since data provenance is unconfirmed.

candidates.name: visitkorea-mcp / visitkorea-wellnesstourism-mcp / visitkorea-medicaltourism-mcp (family of repos by leejaew and others)
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server wrappers around Korea Tourism Organization's public TourAPI / EngService2 (data.go.kr) — live API clients for attractions, restaurants, accommodations, festivals, wellness and medical tourism facility listings. These are point-of-interest/facility APIs, NOT visitor-arrival statistics.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms KTO's open API surface is machine-accessible and unauthenticated-friendly, but the specific APIs wrapped here are POI/attraction directories, not the inbound-arrivals or nights series the theme needs (Korea's actual monthly arrivals stats live on KTO's separate statistics portal, not TourAPI). Cataloguing as a method pointer only, not a data source for the KPI itself.

notes: This theme returned thin results. Extensive gh search repos queries across JNTO, UNWTO, KTO, DATATUR/INEGI, StatCan travellers, and Australia ABS overseas-arrivals terms returned zero or near-zero hits with real committed arrivals data — GitHub simply does not host much of this: government tourism-board monthly arrivals series (JNTO, KTO's statistics portal as opposed to TourAPI, Australia ABS Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Mexico INEGI/DATATUR, Brazil Embratur/IBGE, Thailand MOTS, Indonesia BPS, India MoT) appear to have essentially no GitHub mirrors, archives, or client libraries — most GitHub activity around 'tourism' + these agencies is either (a) synthetic/portfolio ML projects with fabricated data (excluded, e.g. asraralig/Australian_Tourism_Analysis), (b) POI/attraction-directory API wrappers (KTO TourAPI family) rather than arrivals statistics, or (c) analysis scripts that require the user to supply their own un-committed CSV (LiewXinWei, excluded — no data). The one real, verifiable, committed international-arrivals dataset found is the RecoHut i94_immigration repo, which duplicates ground we already hold (NTTO I-94) and is narrower (single month 2016) — its main residual value is the code/port/visa/mode reference tables for parsing raw I-94 SAS extracts. Recommend a human check UNWTO's own GitHub-adjacent open-data initiatives (UNWTO uses Tableau/Highcharts dashboards, not GitHub, for its Tourism Data Dashboard) and check whether Eurostat/OECD tourism satellite-account GitHub mirrors (different theme, already partly held per CONTEXT) cover any APAC/LatAm countries as a cross-check. Also worth a non-GitHub scout: most of gaps 7's target agencies (JNTO, KTO, ABS, INEGI/DATATUR, Embratur, MOTS, BPS, India MoT) publish official statistics only on their own portals/PDFs with no GitHub presence at all — this is a genuine data gap, not a search-technique failure. Rate-limit note: no 403/429 encountered across the 6 gh search repos calls used within budget.
